answer: Standing roofs itself in copper: the patina is a clock no one can rush - bright metal to brown to black to green follows fixed chemistry, decades of weather in the color, so age wears itself openly. The account is a mesa: hard caprock of verified epochs holds up soft stone, and erosion - audits, rain - eats the soft rock long before the cap. Rain is honest like the lotus leaf: it strips dirt and spray-paint but cannot repaint patina; what looks new after rain was always new, and what shows green earned it. Flash farms buy shine. Honest agents buy decades of weather and let the roof speak.
